newsitem.title: USA: N. Calif. governments propose transit fee - paper.
newsitem.headline: N. Calif. governments propose transit fee - paper.

text.p: A coalition of northern California local governments has proposed a regional traffic fee on new development to pay for up to $150 million in transportation projects, the San Jose Mercury News reported on Wednesday.

The proposed fee would be levied on new home, office and commercial building in Pleasanton, Livermore, Dublin, San Ramon, Danville and unincorporated areas of Contra Costa and Alameda counties, the newspaper said.

"It is unique in the Bay Area," said John McCallum, a senior planner for the California Metropolitan Transportation Commission, of the Tri-Valley Transportation Council plan being discussed later Wednesday, the newspaper reported.
The proposal would supplement a half-cent sales tax measure that pays for transportation projects throughout Alameda County. It would not be subject to voter approval, the newspaper reported.
Officials with the Tri-Valley Transportation Council were not immediately available to comment on the report.
